enonce.texte:
Match the verbs with the nouns to form common collocations.

VerbNoun
makea shower
takea decision
doa mistake
haveresearch

questions.texte: Match the verbs with the correct nouns.
questions.reponse: make - a decision, take - a shower, do - research, have - a mistake (INCORRECT: have - breakfast, not a mistake). Correct match: make - a mistake, take - a shower, do - research, have - breakfast.

sousQuestions.texte: Write a sentence using each collocation.
sousQuestions.reponse: Example: 'I need to make a decision about my future. She took a shower after the gym. He does research on climate change. We had breakfast at 8 AM.'

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences with the correct adjective-noun collocation from the box.

box: heavy rain, strong coffee, fast food, deep sleep, strong argument, heavy traffic

  1. There was ________ on the road this morning.
  2. I like to drink ________ in the morning.
  3. We don't eat ________ because it's unhealthy.
  4. After a long day, I fell into a ________.
  5. She made a ________ to support her position.
  6. We got caught in ________ on our way home.

questions.texte: Fill in the blanks with the correct collocations.
questions.reponse: 1. heavy traffic, 2. strong coffee, 3. fast food, 4. deep sleep, 5. strong argument, 6. heavy rain

enonce.texte:
Find and correct the collocation errors in these sentences. These are common mistakes made by French speakers.

  1. He passed the test with high success.
  2. She has a big experience in marketing.
  3. I have a good news for you.
  4. He gave me an important advice.
  5. She is very strong at mathematics.
  6. We enjoyed a large number of food at the party.

questions.texte: Correct the collocation errors in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. He passed the test with great success. 2. She has a lot of experience in marketing. 3. I have good news for you. 4. He gave me important advice. 5. She is very good at mathematics. 6. We enjoyed a lot of food at the party.

sousQuestions.reponse: In English, we say 'a lot of experience' or 'much experience,' not 'big experience.' 'Big' is not used with abstract nouns like 'experience.'

enonce.texte:
Write a short paragraph (5-7 sentences) about your daily work or study routine. Use at least six verb-noun collocations from the list below.

List: make a decision, take a break, do research, have a meeting, give a presentation, take notes, make progress, do a task, have lunch, take responsibility

questions.texte: Write a paragraph using verb-noun collocations.
questions.reponse: Example: 'Every morning, I have a meeting with my team. We discuss our goals and make decisions about new projects. I do research on market trends. During the day, I give a presentation to the managers. I take notes during important discussions. I take a break at noon. I always make progress on my tasks. I take responsibility for my work and ensure everything is done well.'

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences with the correct adverb-adjective collocation. Choose from: deeply disappointed, extremely important, highly successful, strongly opposed, widely known, perfectly clear

  1. The new policy is ________ to the company's future.
  2. She was ________ when she didn't get the job.
  3. The artist is ________ for his beautiful paintings.
  4. Many people are ________ to the new law.
  5. The instructions were ________ and easy to follow.
  6. The campaign was ________ and reached many people.

questions.texte: Fill in the blanks with the correct collocations.
questions.reponse: 1. extremely important, 2. deeply disappointed, 3. widely known, 4. strongly opposed, 5. perfectly clear, 6. highly successful

enonce.texte:
Replace the informal collocations with more formal ones in the following sentences.

  1. We need to think about the problem.
  2. The company wants to look into the issue.
  3. I will give you the report later.
  4. We should talk about the budget.
  5. The team will come up with a solution.
  6. They put forward a proposal.

questions.texte: Replace the informal collocations with formal alternatives.
questions.reponse: 1. We need to consider the problem. 2. The company wants to investigate the issue. 3. I will provide you with the report later. 4. We should discuss the budget. 5. The team will develop a solution. 6. They presented a proposal.

sousQuestions.texte: Why is it important to use formal collocations in professional writing?
sousQuestions.reponse: Formal collocations sound more professional and are appropriate for business emails, reports, and academic writing.

intitule: Writing a Professional Email Using Collocations

enonce.texte:
Write a professional email to your manager. Use at least eight collocations from the list below.

List: make a decision, take responsibility, do research, have a meeting, give a presentation, take notes, make progress, discuss a proposal, consider a solution, provide feedback, submit a report, meet a deadline, handle a problem, address a concern

questions.texte: Write a professional email using collocations.
questions.reponse:
Subject: Update on Project Progress

Dear Mr. Smith,

I am writing to provide an update on the project. We have made significant progress this week. I did research on the market trends and submitted a report to the team. We had a meeting to discuss the proposal. I gave a presentation on our findings. I take responsibility for addressing the concerns raised by the client. I will consider a solution and provide feedback by Friday. I am confident we will meet the deadline.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

enonce.texte:
Read the paragraph and correct the collocation errors.

"Yesterday, I had a big decision to make. I did a lot of research and take a meeting with my manager. She gave me a good advice. I am strong at problem-solving. We made a progress on the project. I felt a deep happy about the results. I hope to do more success in the future."

questions.texte: Find and correct the collocation errors in the paragraph.
questions.reponse: 'had a big decision' → 'had an important decision'; 'take a meeting' → 'had a meeting'; 'gave me a good advice' → 'gave me good advice'; 'I am strong at' → 'I am good at'; 'made a progress' → 'made progress'; 'a deep happy' → 'deep happiness'; 'do more success' → 'achieve more success.'

enonce.texte: Create your own collocation dictionary for the following topics: Work, Travel, and Health. For each topic, list eight collocations (including verb-noun, adjective-noun, and adverb-adjective combinations).

questions.texte: Create a collocation dictionary for three topics.
questions.reponse: Example: Work: make a decision, take responsibility, do research, have a meeting, give a presentation, take notes, make progress, meet a deadline. Travel: book a flight, take a trip, go on vacation, pack a suitcase, visit a country, check into a hotel, rent a car, explore a city. Health: take medicine, do exercise, have a check-up, eat healthy food, get enough sleep, feel exhausted, suffer from stress, maintain a balanced diet.

  2. faire des recherches

  5. prendre des notes
  6. faire du progrès
  7. prendre une pause

questions.texte: Translate the French expressions into English collocations.
questions.reponse: 1. make a decision, 2. do research, 3. have a meeting, 4. give a presentation, 5. take notes, 6. make progress, 7. take a break, 8. have an appointment

sousQuestions.texte: Why is it important to use the correct collocation rather than direct translation?
sousQuestions.reponse: Direct translation often leads to unnatural or incorrect English. Native speakers use fixed combinations that sound natural, so learning collocations improves fluency and accuracy.
